name: Fithir

attributes.attribute: an Irish heroine of great beauty
wed Dairine after Fithir was refused
imprisoned with her handmaidens in a tower

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fithir was an Irish heroine. Her beauty drew the gaze of the king of Leinster. Her father Tuathal Techtmar refused to give her away. He forced the king to marry instead her older sister, Dairine. Then Dairine died, or so the king claimed. He came back and asked for Fithir once more. On this second request, her family agreed. Fithir soon found that her sister was not truly dead. Dairine lay shut in a tall tower ringed by dark woods, held with her handmaidens. Hit by shock and shame, Fithir died.

okr.objective: Fithir is the Irish heroine whose death came from the betrayal of her sister.
key_results: Fithir was an Irish heroine noted for her beauty.
Her father refused her hand to the king of Leinster.
The king married her older sister Dairine instead.
Fithir died of shock and shame when she learned the truth.
